To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mining patterns composed of items with arbitrary attribute combinations is a new challenge, the attribute combinations that define items provide the structural information about a pattern, and the structural information of a pattern is a valuable source for mining efficiency improvement.
the structural relationships among patterns in large relational tables can be exploited for mining, and that this approach can reduce mining time substantially.

the structure of patterns in a large relational database can be exploited in mining to reduce the number of patterns to consider, and that the interrelationships among the patterns can be used to further reduce the number of candidate patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mining of associations in a large relational database.
mining patterns that describe the relationships between attributes in a large database table, and with organizing the mining space based upon the structural information of patterns.
the problem of mining associations by pattern structure from large, relational databases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to reduce the mining time by 30% to 70% compared to the state-of-the-art algorithms.
the proposed architecture is able to mine patterns with a wide range of pattern structures efficiently, while the current association algorithms cannot.
the proposed architecture can effectively organize the mining space, which can significantly reduce the execution time for mining association patterns in large relational tables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for association rule mining that can be applied to any relational table, regardless of the number of attributes, their types, and their relationships.
the pattern structures are useful and can be efficiently exploited for mining.
we have developed a novel approach to organize mining space for association mining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mining of patterns in large relational tables should be guided by the structural information of patterns.
the structural information in patterns can be exploited to organize and reduce the mining space, and hence to improve mining efficiency.
pattern structures can be used to improve the mining performance.
